tei:titleStmt.tei:title: אִם אָפֵס רֹֽבַע הַקֵּן
Im Afes Rova' ha-Qen, by Rabbi Ephraim bar Isaac of Regensburg, ca. 12th c. (rhyming Ladino translation by Rabbi Reuven Eliyahu Yisrael of Craiova, 1910)

tei:div.tei:head: Im Afes Rova' ha-Qen, by Rabbi Ephraim bar Isaac of Regensburg, ca. 12th c. (rhyming Ladino translation by Rabbi Reuven Eliyahu Yisrael of Craiova, 1910)

tei:lg.tei:l: Though the service of sacrifices be abandoned,
though our sanctuary be desecrated,
the people of Israel shall never be exterminated,
due to the revered patriarch Abraham.
His devotion, o God, recognize,
his faithfulness always remember,
when You said to him: “Take your given son and slit his throat,
and pour his blood upon the altar.”
Abraham quickly ran to prepare his son,
of whom his soul was bound to his soul in a strong bond.
He prepared the wood and the fire as God wanted,
without Isaac knowing the purpose of that fire.
Swift as a roe deer, Isaac submitted to his command.
To his father he said: “Have you forgotten?
The fire and the wood we are already carrying;
where is the animal whose throat will be slit?”
Then his father, so as not to upset him,
answered his son, to satisfy him:
“God will prepare the animal to have its throat slit.
We must walk and wait for it.”
Father and son, with great devotion,
continued their paths with purity and sanctification,
doing God‘s will their only thought,
Crossing mountains with haste.
When they saw from the east
that a cloud was descending and settling on the mountain,
they prepared the logs with an ardent love
to do the will of the Omnipotent God.
When Isaac understood that he was to be sacrificed,
he said to his very elderly father:
“My father, tie me up like a lamb, fastened well.
Don’t be merciful, even though I was given to you.
God chose me and wanted me to merit it.
we cannot defy Them! We must obey.
A mortal’s end this must be,
to die, to disappear from among the living.”
With strength and courage, obeying his God,
Abraham bound his son, born to him at a hundred years old,
and spread him out on top of the wood
and kindled the fire on the altar.
His throat stretched out without hesitation,
and his father circled around him with intention,
to slit his throat and offer him upward,
and God watched him with attention.
What this father did was shocking:
without any mercy, he was going to cut down his son,
to offer him as a sacrifice on the altar,
to carry out the order of his God and to respect it.
As Abraham put the knife to his throat,
a voice from heaven called out aloud:
“Abraham, Abraham! Do not touch the young man, stop,
Slit the throat of that ram and untie Isaac.
This animal is to be his replacement,
destined for this since birth.
Already I knew the purity of your feeling,
your loyalty and your devotion.”
May the memory of this act, o God, be before Your throne!
Father and son obeyed You with great energy.
Do not forget Your covenant with the Jewish nation;
hear our prayers on this day!
Your faithful children call to you in desperation.
May this important act be their protection;
rescue with Your mercy Your nation
that always awaits your salvation.
